output.myth: Each autumn the grey geese go south in a wedge, and the old women say the wedge is the shape of Kael's net. Kael once cast it over the sea for a fallen star. He never caught one, but the cords stayed in the sky. Tavo raised a gale over the Leeward Reach and drove Hasken's three boats past the last rock, and they never came home. Hesk counted them at the pole and wound a line for each. Ennu had shown those men how to set their sails in a wedge, so the drowned gave the shape to the geese. The lead bird points the way the boats should have come home. Its wedge is always a little crooked, because Hasken's youngest steered badly and the goose has never forgiven him. If you see the wedge over the water, mend your net, count your children, and do not watch too long. The sky keeps what looks at it.
output.verse:
South go the grey geese,
the wedge shows the drowned way home,
mend the net; look away.

judge.advice: Keep the composition, but tidy it. (1) Move the breast star 23835 from about (331,265) down to about (340,290) so it sits in the body's centre. (2) Strengthen the trailing edge of the left wing: draw the blue wing outline from 25945 (152,264) back to 25278 (208,302) and on to the body near (315,335), so the rear edge is a distinct curve. Do the same for the right wing from 22565 (446,257) back toward the body. (3) Stop the right-wingtip-to-tail-tip gold edge from defining the silhouette; either curve the right wing's trailing edge inward or shorten that line so the tail reads as a separate feature. (4) Shorten or relocate the labels: put 'left wingtip' above the wing, put 'belly' to the left of its star and 'base of tail' to the right, and abbreviate the head label to 'head & beak'. (5) Keep the unlabelled stars at (300,344) and (442,397) dimmer so they are not read as key stars. Verdict stays keep under the rule (match 4, fit 3), but the adjustments above would raise fit.
